## The Fproxy rule

The (Icelandic) rule is conventionally written as:

$C = F_{proxy}I$

ICES prefers to introduce it in this form:

$C = I F_{proxy}bm$

When relating this to the fundamental fisheries equation:

$C_y = F_y B_y$

and/or it's illusive derivative:

$MSY = F_{MSY}B_{MSY}$

we rearrange:

$C = (mbF_{proxy})I$

Now the b here is just:

$b = min(1, I_y/Itrigger)$

Ergo, besides the $m$ the rule is just another form of the icod advisory rule, where

$I = qB$

which means effectively that the $q$ gets embedded in the $F_{proxy}$. Just to derive it from fundamental equation:

$C_y = F_y B_y$

$C_y = F_y I_y/q$

$C_y = (F_y/q) I_y$

$C_y = F_{proxy}I_y$

Including the sliding part into the advisory rule we have:

$C_y = (min(1, I_y/I_{trigger})F_{proxy})I_y$

Including the $m$ term in the ICES Fproxy rule is really just to create confusion. It is a time invariant parameter (just like $I_{trigger}$ and $F_{proxy}$) and hence should be included in the derivation of $F_{proxy}$, i.e.:

$F_{proxy} = mF_{init}$

Now, I challenge anybody to derive ICES ratio rule from the principle equation.

## cod - length based proxies

```{r SETTINGS}
sid <- 1
tac <- 223
tac_lastyear <- 250
prev_fproxy <- 0.2 # not really
tegund_k <- 0.1    # from Muggur's presentation (2021/07 WKILIFE Subgroup)
linf <- 150
calc_linf <- FALSE
lbinwidth <- 1     # bindwidths
apply_precuationary_buffer <- FALSE
mfdb <- c('BMT', 'LLN', 'GIL')

assyear <- lubridate::now() %>% lubridate::year()
lastyear <- assyear - 1
```

```{r DATA}
# Commercial length distributions ----------------------------------------------
ldist.year <-
  ldist_by_year(con, sampling_type = c(1,2,8), species_nr = sid) %>%
  filter(mfdb_gear_code %in% mfdb) %>%
  filter(year %in% 1975:lastyear) %>% 
  group_by(year, length) %>%
  summarise(n = sum(n, na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  collect(n = Inf) %>% 
  as_tibble() %>% 
  # some lengths may not be on whole cm bins
  mutate(length = floor(length)) %>% 
  group_by(year, length) %>% 
  summarise(n = sum(n),
            .groups = "drop") %>% 
  filter(length <= linf)
if(calc_linf) linf <- max(ldist.year$length) # not really
# reference values each year
lref.year <- 
  ldist.year %>%
  group_by(year) %>% 
  summarise(lc = dlsrules:::dl_1st_capture(length, n),
            lt = dl_target(lc, linf),
            lm = dlsrules:::dl_mean(length, n, lc),
            .groups = "drop")
```


```{r}
#| fig.cap = "Icelandic cod. Length at first capture (lc), mean length above
#|  first capture (lm) and 'annual' target length (lt)."
lref.year %>% 
  gather(var, val, -year) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(year, val, colour = var)) + 
  geom_line(lwd = 1) +
  scale_colour_brewer(palette = "Set1") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Length [cm]",
       colour = "ref F")
```


```{r}
lref <- 
  lref.year %>% 
  summarise(lc = median(lc),
            lt = median(lt),
            lm = median(lm))
lref.year %>% 
  select(-lt) %>% 
  mutate(f = lm / lref$lt) %>% 
  select(year, lm, f) %>% 
  gather(var, val, -year) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(year, val)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_hline(data = tibble(y = c(1, lref$lt), 
                           var = c("f", "lm")),
             aes(yintercept = y)) +
  facet_grid(var ~ ., scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL)
```


```{r}
#| fig.cap = "Annual mean length above Lc and estimated fishing mortality."
rby <- 
  fishvice::fv_rbx("/u2/reikn/Tac/2022/01-cod/ass/mup/smx", scale = 1000)$rby %>%   select(year, bio, fbar, rec = r, catch = oY) %>% 
  filter(between(year, 1975, 2021))
rby %>% 
  select(year, fbar) %>% 
  left_join(lref.year %>% 
              select(year, lm)) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(fbar, lm)) +
  geom_path() +
  geom_point(aes(colour = factor(year))) +
  scale_colour_viridis_d() +
  theme(legend.position = "none") +
  labs(x = "Fbar", y = "Mean length above Lc") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = lref$lt) +
  annotate("text", x = 1, y = lref$lt + 1, label = "Ltarget", hjust = 1) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0.3) +
  annotate("text", x = 0.27, y = 64, label = "Ftarget", hjust = 0, angle = 90)
```

## Age based proxies

We will test the DLS rules (rfb and the fproxy rule) on cod using the age based analytical assessment that is currently used to derive the annual advice.

## Preamble

By reference to "Poor man's" it means that the testing done is using hindcasting of data-rich [sic] age-based assessements. The idea is to use the analytical estimates of recruitment patterns, run those through hindcasting by applying some ~msy fishing pressure, use some age proxy for estimating contemporanous **"f"**, use biomass estimates to calculate the 2-over-3 ration (with or without adding noise), etc.


```{r}
#  get data
rbx <-
  fishvice::mup_rbx("/u2/reikn/Tac/2022/01-cod/ass/mup/smx", scale = 1000)
rbx$rbya <-
  rbx$rbya %>%
  mutate(mat = replace_na(mat, 0),
         mat = ifelse(age >= 4, 1, 0),
         ssbW = cW,                    # 2022-05-28 from cW to sW as in paper
         ssbW = replace_na(ssbW, 0))
fls <-
  rbx %>%
  rbx_to_flstock(pf = 0, pm = 0, fage = c(5, 10)) %>%
  FLCore::trim(year = 1955:2022)

# hindcast with fbar = 0.3 (~ Fmsy)
hind <- fwd(fls,
            sr = rec(fls)[, ac(1960:2022)],
            control = fwdControl(year = 1960:2022,
                                 value = 0.3,
                                 quant = "fbar"))
```

```{r}
#| fig.cap = "Current assessment (spaly) and hindcasting from 1960 using an
#|  ftarget rate of 0.30."
plot(FLStocks(spaly = fls, hind = hind)) +
  theme_bw() +
  geom_line(lwd = 1) +
  scale_colour_brewer(palette = "Set1") +
  labs(colour = "Run")
```

### DLS rules

The approch here is to use the reference biomass estimate ($B_{4+}$) as a survey index ($I$). This is equivalent of assuming that the catchability ($q$) in the following equation is 1:

$U_y = qB_y$

And instead of deriving the $f_{target}$ from length we will cook up some age based target proxy instead. In the hindcasting above we ran the assessment forward based on $F_{5-10} = F_{msy} = 0.30$. Hence we should have the age composition in the fisheries when fishing at $F_{msy}$. Lets derive the Ac and Atarget similarily as done using length data:

```{r}
rbya <- 
  hind %>% 
  flstock_to_rbya()
ainf <- 16
aref.year <- 
  rbya %>%
  group_by(year) %>% 
  summarise(ac = dlsrules:::dl_1st_capture(age, oC),
            at = dl_target(ac, ainf),
            am = dlsrules:::dl_mean(age, oC, ac),
            .groups = "drop")
aref.year %>% 
  gather(var, val, -year) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(year, val, colour = var)) + 
  geom_line(lwd = 1) +
  scale_colour_brewer(palette = "Set1") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Length [cm]",
       colour = "ref F")
aref <-
  aref.year %>% 
  drop_na() %>% 
  summarise(ac = mean(ac),
            at = mean(at),
            am = mean(am))
aref
```

So basically our target age (mean age in catch **greater than** the age of first capture (age4)) is 7.05. This is the denominator when deriving the annual **f**.

```{r}
# We need at least 5 years of survey data in order to start using the rfb-rule
stk <- fls %>% FLCore::trim(year = 1955:1959)
rec <- fls %>% rec() %>% trim(year = 1960:2022)
fmsy_age_proxy <- aref$at 
for(y in 1960:2022) {
  
  yc.last <- as.character(y - 1)
  yc <- as.character(y)
  #print(yc)
  
  last.year <- range(stk)["maxyear"][[1]]
  this.year <- last.year + 1
  current.catch <- catch(stk) %>% last()
  amean <-
    catch.n(stk)[, yc.last] %>%
    as.data.frame() %>%
    as_tibble() %>%
    filter(age > 4) %>%
    summarise(x = sum(age * data) / sum(data)) %>%
    pull(x)
  f <- amean / fmsy_age_proxy
  bio <- computeStock(stk) %>% as.vector() %>% rev()
  b2 <- mean(bio[1:2])
  b3 <- mean(bio[3:5])
  r <- b2/b3
  
  m <- 0.90
  next.advice <- r * m * f * current.catch
  next.advice <- min(max(0.7 * current.catch, next.advice), 1.2 * current.catch)
  # note: should really take the "real" weights
  proj <- stf(stk, nyears = 1, wts.nyears = 1)
  ctrl <-
    fwdControl(data.frame(year = this.year,
                          quant = "catch",
                          value = next.advice))
  stk <- fwd(proj, control = ctrl, sr = rec[,yc])
  
}
plot(FLStocks(spaly = fls, hind = hind, dls23 = stk)) +
  theme_bw() +
  geom_line(lwd = 1) +
  scale_colour_brewer(palette = "Set1")
```
